findings.claim: cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md § 2 'New Features by Domain' enumerates 83 features with an 'Owning domain' column, but the file's own Downstream contract assigns a disposition only to § 1 and § 3, leaving § 2 with no stated consumer, no MoSCoW placement, and no owning feature file. Verified: the 83 never landed anywhere downstream.
findings.evidence: meta/cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md:7-10 — "**Downstream contract**: `/create-prd` (architecture + shared-mechanism registry), `/decompose-architecture` (domain/shard boundaries), and `/audit-ambiguity` inherit this file. The **New Cross-Cut Mechanisms** table is the authoritative \"extract-me-as-shared\" list — anything here must NOT be rebuilt per-domain. The **Boundary Analysis** section is the D-17 verdict." — § 2 is the only one of the three sections given no disposition. meta/cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md:129-133 — "## 2. New Features by Domain" / "Deduped from 90 candidates." meta/cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md:135 header "| Feature | Owning domain | Why it's new / uncovered |" over 83 rows (lines 137-219), e.g. :157 "| Rights-Orphan Detector | 07 | A readiness check flagging a Song at `master approved` with ZERO asserted recordings in 09 ... The loudest completeness deficit"; :202 "| Postponement as a first-class booking state | 17 | The date moves, the deal survives, tickets stay valid — post-2020 the dominant outcome"; :166 "| Medley / multi-work composition object | 09 | ... No feature covers medley composition."; :219 "| Formula / contingent receivable | 23 | ... 23.03 models no unknown-amount/formula-shaped receivables". The closing instruction at :268-272 commissions only the § 1 extractions and the § 3 merge/relocation decisions — § 2 is not carried forward. VERIFICATION: grep -ril over the entire non-meta ideation tree returns 0 files for 'orphan', 'postpone', 'medley', 'test mix|test-mix', and 'save the venue|save-the-venue'; feature-ledger.md returns 0 for 'Rights-Orphan', 'orphan', 'medley', 'Save-the-venue' and 'Trial / test-mix' (its single 'postpone' hit, line 417 `19.06.03` Reschedule & Postponement Handling / Should, is a different, pre-existing feature — the § 2 entry is 'Postponement as a first-class booking state' owned by 17, which the file says is neither cancellation nor force majeure). So none of the 83 is in a domain feature file or in the 734-feature ledger, while ideation-index.md:154 scores Feature Completeness ✅ on "195 Musts at `[DEEP]` ... 734 features in feature-ledger.md" and constraints.md:197-244 allocates exactly 195 Musts across v1 (~45) / v1.5 (~26) / phase 2+ (~124) with none of the 83 accounted for.
findings.forcedInvention: Whether the 83 § 2 features are in scope, and at what MoSCoW level and in which release, is not stated anywhere. /decompose-architecture and /plan-phase must invent it. Reading the same unit, one implementer folds all 83 into the domain feature files as new scope (changing the 195-Must accounting and the v1/v1.5/phase-2 split); another treats § 2 as an advisory gap log already superseded by the § 1 mechanism extractions and builds none of them. That is a ~11% swing on a 734-feature corpus, decided by nothing in the text.
findings.short_summary: 83 emergent features in §2 have no stated disposition or MoSCoW

findings.claim: constraints.md and competitive-landscape.md each self-declare status `[DEEP]` with a completion date, while the Structure Map in ideation-index.md records both as `[PARTIAL]`. Neither side carries a marker reconciling the two, and the same tree marks problem-statement.md `[DEEP]` in both places despite it also carrying open questions — so the divergence is not explained by a consistent convention.
findings.evidence: meta/constraints.md:3 — "> Status: `[DEEP]` — all constraint categories resolved during `/ideate-validate` 2026-07-18." versus ideation-index.md:95 — "| Constraints | [constraints.md](meta/constraints.md) | `[PARTIAL]` |". meta/competitive-landscape.md:3 — "> Status: `[DEEP]` — completed `/ideate-validate` 2026-07-18." versus ideation-index.md:94 — "| Competitive Landscape | [competitive-landscape.md](meta/competitive-landscape.md) | `[PARTIAL]` |". The index table is introduced at ideation-index.md:85 as "> Downstream workflows: read this table to find the specific file you need." Counter-evidence that the index is not applying a stricter 'open questions remain' sense of the marker: ideation-index.md:91 records problem-statement.md as `[DEEP]` although that file carries an explicitly `[PARTIAL]` section (problem-statement.md:71 — "`[PARTIAL]` — the strongest candidate signals, to be confirmed with the owner") and two live owner questions; and ideation-index.md:157 self-scores Competitive Positioning ✅ citing the same competitive-landscape.md it marks `[PARTIAL]`.
findings.failure_scenario: A downstream stage that gates on the Structure Map status treats constraints.md and competitive-landscape.md as incomplete and either re-opens settled constraint axes or blocks on them; a stage that reads the files directly treats both as resolved inputs and proceeds. The locked technical constraints (constraints.md:11-17) and the release plan (constraints.md:197-244) are the single most load-bearing inputs to /create-prd-stack and /plan-phase, so the two readings produce different pipeline behaviour on the most consequential file in the unit.
findings.short_summary: Index says [PARTIAL]; constraints.md and competitive-landscape.md say [DEEP]

findings.claim: competitive-landscape.md's Moat section asserts the earned-vs-hostile lock-in answer as settled positioning, with no provisional marker, while problem-statement.md holds that exact question open as an owner decision (Q-02) and records the matching Deep Think hypothesis as deferred (DT-04). The compiled vision.md repeats the assertion, so the open question is either stale or the position is unratified — and nothing in the unit says which.
findings.evidence: meta/competitive-landscape.md:82-85 — "**Earned lock-in, not hostile lock-in.** The moat is the accumulating, verified record of a musician's career ... A user who leaves doesn't lose access to *data they could export*; they lose the *provenance* that only exists because the platform was in the workflow when the work happened." versus meta/problem-statement.md:112 — "| Q-02 | [OWNER] Is the lock-in **earned** or **hostile**? If a user leaves, what do they take? (Data portability is a cross-cut — and a values decision.) | User | `/create-prd` |" and meta/problem-statement.md:105 — "| DT-04 | \"Cannot live without\" comes from accumulated switching cost | Sweep whitespace lens | ⏳ DEFERRED — must confirm lock-in is *earned* (value they'd miss) not *hostile* (data they can't extract). See Q-02 |". The Moat text answers Q-02's second clause verbatim ('what do they take?' -> 'data they could export'). Corroboration that the assertion has propagated as settled: vision.md:53 — "It is the earned lock-in the whole product is built to create." Note also that vision.md's canonical Open Questions table (vision.md:219-228) does not carry problem-statement.md's Q-02 at all, and reuses the identifier Q-02 for an unrelated question (vision.md:221 — "| Q-02 | The identifier-binding seam — which mechanism/domain owns work↔identifier binding? | Agent |"). Contrast the file's own handling of a genuinely resolved question, which is struck through and marked: problem-statement.md:113 — "| Q-03 | ~~...~~ **RESOLVED (D-31):** ... | User | ✅ Resolved |".
findings.failure_scenario: Data portability and export scope is a product decision that follows directly from this answer. An implementer reading competitive-landscape.md (or vision.md) builds to 'users can export their data, the moat is the unexportable provenance' and specs export surfaces into v1; an implementer reading problem-statement.md sees a live [OWNER] values decision deferred to /create-prd and specs nothing, waiting for the owner. Because Q-02 is absent from vision.md's canonical roll-up, the /create-prd stage that is supposed to resolve it may never be handed it, and the unratified assertion silently becomes the decision.
findings.short_summary: Moat asserts earned lock-in while Q-02/DT-04 keep it open
